title_es: Template literals y métodos de cadena en JavaScript
title_en: Template literals and string methods in JavaScript
body_es: Los template literals (backticks) permiten crear strings que pueden contener expresiones usando ${}: `Hola ${name}`. Son más legibles que la concatenación tradicional con +. También permiten strings multilínea nativamente. Los métodos de cadena comunes incluyen `toUpperCase()` y `toLowerCase()` para cambiar caso. `trim()` elimina espacios en blanco. `split()` divide un string en un array. `join()` hace lo opuesto. `replace()` cambia la primera ocurrencia de un patrón. `replaceAll()` cambia todas las ocurrencias. `includes()`, `startsWith()`, `endsWith()` comprueban si un string contiene texto. `substring()` y `slice()` extraen partes de strings. `padStart()` y `padEnd()` agregan caracteres. `repeat()` repite un string. Estos métodos son esenciales para procesar y formatear texto. Los template literals son preferidos en JavaScript moderno por su legibilidad y funcionalidad.
body_en: Template literals (backticks) allow creating strings that can contain expressions using ${}: `Hello ${name}`. They are more readable than traditional concatenation with +. They also support multi-line strings natively. Common string methods include `toUpperCase()` and `toLowerCase()` for changing case. `trim()` removes whitespace. `split()` divides a string into an array. `join()` does the opposite. `replace()` changes the first occurrence of a pattern. `replaceAll()` changes all occurrences. `includes()`, `startsWith()`, `endsWith()` check if a string contains text. `substring()` and `slice()` extract parts of strings. `padStart()` and `padEnd()` add characters. `repeat()` repeats a string. These methods are essential for processing and formatting text. Template literals are preferred in modern JavaScript for their readability and functionality.
